# Investigation: `Context.res` setter header merging (Hono 4.13.18)

Read-only investigation. No source or test files were modified. The only file added is this document.

Scope: how the `Context.res` setter merges response headers when assigning a `Response`, with
special attention to `Set-Cookie`, the call sites that reach it, existing test coverage, and the
risks of changing the behavior.

Method: static reading of `src/context.ts` and its callers/tests, plus a small runtime probe of the
platform `Headers` implementation (`entries()` / `getSetCookie()`). The test suite was not executed.

---

## 1. Primary implementation

### 1.1 Getter that seeds the "old" response

`src/context.ts:403-407`

```ts
get res(): Response {
  return (this.#res ||= createResponseInstance(null, {
    headers: (this.#preparedHeaders ??= new Headers()),
  }))
}
```

The getter lazily creates `#res` from `#preparedHeaders`. `#preparedHeaders` is where `c.header()`
writes before any response exists (`src/context.ts:519-532`, selection at `:524`). So the "old"
headers merged by the setter can be either:

- headers previously set through `c.header(...)` that were promoted into `#res`, or
- headers on a previously assigned/created `Response`.

`createResponseInstance` is just `new Response(body, init)` (`src/context.ts:288-291`).

### 1.2 The setter

`src/context.ts:414-434`

```ts
set res(_res: Response | undefined) {
  if (this.#res && _res) {
    _res = createResponseInstance(_res.body, _res)
    for (const [k, v] of this.#res.headers.entries()) {
      if (k === 'content-type') {
        continue
      }
      if (k === 'set-cookie') {
        const cookies = this.#res.headers.getSetCookie()
        _res.headers.delete('set-cookie')
        for (const cookie of cookies) {
          _res.headers.append('set-cookie', cookie)
        }
      } else {
        _res.headers.set(k, v)
      }
    }
  }
  this.#res = _res
  this.finalized = true
}
```

Key facts:

1. **Merge only happens when both an old and a new response exist** (`:415`). If `#res` is unset,
   the new response is stored as-is. If `_res` is `undefined`, the setter clears `#res` and marks the
   context finalized (`:432-433`). Clearing then re-setting is a supported reset pattern
   (`src/hono.test.ts:1204-1208`).
2. **The new response is cloned before mutation** (`:416`). This is what makes it safe to assign
   responses whose headers are immutable (e.g. a `fetch()` response); mutating `_res.headers`
   directly would throw `TypeError`. Covered by `src/context.test.ts:468-488`.
3. **`Content-Type` is deliberately skipped** (`:418-420`), so the new response keeps its own
   content type instead of inheriting the old one.
4. **`Set-Cookie` is special-cased** (`:421-426`): all old cookies are read with `getSetCookie()`,
   every `set-cookie` on the new response is deleted, then the old cookies are appended. **New
   response cookies are discarded; only the old/context cookies survive.**
5. **Every other header is overwritten by the old value** via `set` (`:428`), i.e. old wins for
   duplicate names. Header names from `entries()` are lowercase, and `Headers.set` is
   case-insensitive, so casing is not an issue for this branch.

### 1.3 Exact merge order (old = `this.#res`, new = argument)

```
if old && new:
  new = new Response(new.body, new)          # context.ts:416
  for (k, v) in old.headers.entries():       # context.ts:417
    if k == "content-type":  continue        # :418-420   -> new wins
    if k == "set-cookie":                    # :421
      oldCookies = old.headers.getSetCookie()# :422       -> old only
      new.headers.delete("set-cookie")       # :423       -> new cookies dropped
      for c in oldCookies: new.headers.append("set-cookie", c)  # :424-426
    else:
      new.headers.set(k, v)                  # :428       -> old wins
old = new; finalized = true                  # :432-433
```

Effective precedence:

| Header category | Winner when both define it | Multi-value handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | **new** response (`:418-420`) | single value |
| `Set-Cookie` | **old** context response (`:421-426`) | old cookies preserved via `getSetCookie()`/`append`; new cookies deleted |
| any other header | **old** context response (`:428`) | old `entries()` value is `set`, replacing the new value |

Note on `entries()`: current Node/undici yields one entry per `Set-Cookie` value (duplicate
`set-cookie` keys), while other runtimes may yield a single comma-joined entry. The special case is
written to work either way because it re-reads `getSetCookie()` and deletes before appending; it is
idempotent across duplicate entries.

---

## 2. Call sites of the setter

### 2.1 Framework/core call sites

| Location | Context | Why the merge matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/compose.ts:67-69` | `compose()` assigns `context.res = res` when the returned response exists and the context is not finalized (or an error was handled) | **Main entry point.** Every middleware/handler response flows through the setter. This is where context headers/cookies set earlier are merged into the returned response. |
| `src/hono-base.ts:448-467` (assignment at `:453`) | Single-handler fast path: `c.res = await this.#notFoundHandler(c)` inside the `next()` callback | Applies the same merge to not-found responses; `c.res` is also read at `:463`. |

### 2.2 Built-in middleware call sites

| Location | Assignment |
| --- | --- |
| `src/middleware/trailing-slash/index.ts:71` and `:155` | `c.res = c.redirect(url.toString(), 301)` |
| `src/middleware/method-not-allowed/index.ts:137-139` | `c.res = options.onMethodNotAllowed ?? c.text('Method Not Allowed', 405, ...)` (preceded by deleting `Allow`/`Content-Length` at `:131-133`) |
| `src/middleware/etag/index.ts:119-130` | `c.res = new Response(null, { status: 304, headers: { ETag } })`, then deletes headers not in `RETAINED_304_HEADERS` (`src/middleware/etag/index.ts:21-28`, `:126-130`). The setter first copies the old headers onto the 304, then the middleware prunes them. |
| `src/middleware/pretty-json/index.ts:63-66` | `c.res = new Response(JSON.stringify(...), c.res)` after cancelling the body |
| `src/middleware/compress/index.ts:113-128` | `ctx.res = new Response(ctx.res.body.pipeThrough(stream), ctx.res)`; depends on old headers (including `Vary`, `ETag`, `Set-Cookie`) surviving the reassignment |

### 2.3 Read-side call sites that depend on the merged result

These do not invoke the setter but read/write `c.res.headers` after `next()`, so they rely on the
merge semantics:

- `src/middleware/cors/index.ts:102,120,144,147-151` — sets/appends CORS headers and rebuilds the
  response from `c.res.headers`
- `src/middleware/powered-by/index.ts:33` — `c.res.headers.set('X-Powered-By', ...)`
- `src/middleware/timing/timing.ts:113,119` — appends `Server-Timing`
- `src/middleware/cache/index.ts:233,307-317` — inspects/clones `c.res`; caching explicitly avoids

- If the policy changed to "merge old + new", duplicate cookies could be emitted (same name/path
  from both the context and the handler), producing ambiguous sessions.
- If the policy changed to "new wins", a handler could override or remove a session/CSRF cookie set
  by trusted middleware, and could shadow `__Host-`/`__Secure-` cookies. Prefix behavior is covered
  at `src/helper/cookie/index.test.ts:249-283`.
- Deleting an attacker-influenced handler cookie set is a security-relevant behavior; loosening it
  needs threat modeling.

### 5.3 Immutability and streaming

- The clone at `src/context.ts:416` must be preserved. Refactoring to mutate `_res.headers` directly
  will throw on fetch responses and break `src/context.test.ts:468-488`.
- Re-wrapping `_res.body` must not double-lock an already-used stream; the consumed-body case is
  covered at `src/context.test.ts:497-504`, and `compress`/`pretty-json` cancel/pipe bodies
  (`src/middleware/compress/index.ts:126`, `src/middleware/pretty-json/index.ts:63-64`).

### 5.4 Downstream middleware interactions

- `etag` relies on the setter copying old headers onto the 304 before pruning non-retained ones
  (`src/middleware/etag/index.ts:119-130`; retained set at `:21-28`). A merge change could leak
  headers onto 304s or remove `ETag`/`Vary`/cache headers.
- `cache` clones and inspects `c.res` (`src/middleware/cache/index.ts:307-317`) and deliberately
  refuses to cache responses with `Set-Cookie` (`src/middleware/cache/index.test.ts:500-516`).
  Cookie merge changes could enable cache poisoning or cache misses.
- `cors` rebuilds a response from `c.res.headers` (`src/middleware/cors/index.ts:147-154`), so any
  header lost in the merge disappears from preflight responses.
- `compress` and `pretty-json` assign a rebuilt response and then mutate headers; they assume the
  old headers (including `Vary`, `ETag`, cookies) were carried over.

### 5.5 Runtime portability

- `getSetCookie()` is not uniformly available; the AWS Lambda adapter already feature-detects it
  (`src/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.ts:419-420`). Any new logic must not assume it exists.
- `Headers.entries()` may yield multiple `set-cookie` entries or one comma-joined entry depending on
  the runtime. Logic must remain correct in both cases (the current delete-then-append-all is
  idempotent; a naive `append` without `delete` would duplicate cookies under duplicate keys).

### 5.6 Performance

- Each assignment with an existing `#res` allocates a new `Response`, iterates all old headers, and
  re-reads all cookies. Changing to a per-cookie/merge-map algorithm adds work to a hot path used by
  `compress`, `pretty-json`, `etag`, and every `compose` dispatch. No benchmarks currently guard
  this.

### 5.7 Clearing / undefined semantics

- `c.res = undefined` must remain a full reset (`src/hono.test.ts:1204-1208`). Any new merge logic
  must keep the `!this.#res || !_res` short-circuit in `src/context.ts:415` intact.

---

## 6. If a change is pursued (recommended guardrails)

1. Add characterization tests first, ideally at both the unit level (`Context` directly) and through
   `app.request()` with a real middleware chain, covering:
   - old vs new same-name non-content-type header,
   - new `Set-Cookie` when `#res` already exists,
   - old + new `Set-Cookie` ordering and duplicate names,
   - immutable responses carrying cookies,
   - each built-in middleware listed in Section 2.2.
2. Run the suite across Node, Bun, Deno, and workerd to pin `entries()`/`getSetCookie()` differences.
3. Keep the clone at `src/context.ts:416` and the `Content-Type` skip.
4. Decide the cookie policy explicitly (old-only, old+new, or new-only) and, if merging, define
   de-duplication by cookie name/domain/path. Prefer an opt-in option over changing the default.
5. Reconcile the setter with `#newResponse` (`src/context.ts:609-657`) so the same policy applies
   before and after assignment; today the setter can undo `#newResponse`'s cookie merge.
6. Add a micro-benchmark for repeated `c.res =` assignments.

---

- Middleware assignments: `src/middleware/trailing-slash/index.ts:71,155`;
  `src/middleware/method-not-allowed/index.ts:131-139`; `src/middleware/etag/index.ts:119-130`;
  `src/middleware/pretty-json/index.ts:63-66`; `src/middleware/compress/index.ts:113-128`
- Cookie helpers: `src/helper/cookie/index.ts:99-102,130-139,141-145`
- Tests: `src/context.test.ts:300-311,408-418,430-445,447-454,456-466,468-488,490-504,522-535,578-592`;

Investigation complete. I created `INVESTIGATION.md` (337 lines) at the repo root and left everything else untouched. No `git add`/`git commit` was run; `git status` shows only `INVESTIGATION.md` as a new untracked file alongside the pre-existing untracked tooling directories.

## Key findings

**The setter** (`src/context.ts:414-434`) only merges when both an old `#res` and a new `_res` exist (`:415`). It clones the new response first (`:416`) to avoid mutating immutable fetch headers, then iterates the **old** headers:

| Header category | Winner | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| `Content-Type` | **new** response | skipped at `:418-420`, so the new response keeps its own type |
| `Set-Cookie` | **old** context response | `getSetCookie()` on old (`:422`), delete all new cookies (`:423`), re-append old (`:424-426`) — **new response cookies are discarded** |
| everything else | **old** context response | `_res.headers.set(k, v)` at `:428` overwrites the new value |

**Call sites:** `compose.ts:67-69` (main entry for every middleware/handler response), `hono-base.ts:453` (single-handler notFound), and the built-ins `trailing-slash` (`:71,155`), `method-not-allowed` (`:137`), `etag` (`:119`), `pretty-json` (`:64`), `compress` (`:126`). Cookie producers use `c.header('Set-Cookie', …, { append: true })` (`helper/cookie/index.ts:99-102`).

**Key asymmetry:** `#newResponse` (`src/context.ts:609-657`) merges old + response-argument cookies by *appending*, but if that result is later assigned through `c.res` while `#res` exists, the setter deletes all new `Set-Cookie` and re-appends only the old ones. Existing tests check the returned response directly (`context.test.ts:578-592`), not the post-assignment context — a real coverage gap.

**Test coverage:** cookie retention/new-cookie drop (`context.test.ts:430-445`), content-type precedence (`:408-418`, `:522-535`), immutable headers (`:468-488`), consumed bodies (`:497-504`), middleware reassignment (`hono.test.ts:1196-1224`). Gaps include: no same-name old-vs-new non-cookie header test, no end-to-end `#newResponse`→setter cookie test, no cross-runtime `entries()`/`getSetCookie()` test, and no immutable-response test hitting the cookie branch.

**Risks:** compatibility of "old wins" middleware-header persistence, cookie ordering/security (session, CSRF, `__Host-`/`__Secure-`), immutable-header cloning at `:416`, 304 pruning in `etag`, cache-poisoning interactions, runtime differences in `Set-Cookie` enumeration, and added allocations on a hot path. Guardrails and recommended test matrix are documented in Sections 5–6 of `INVESTIGATION.md`.

Verification note: findings are from static reading plus a runtime probe of `Headers.entries()`/`getSetCookie()`; I did not execute the test suite.
